finding.sequence_description: Direct JWT login: simulate signing-key rotation by changing jwt_validation_pubkeys after a successful control login, then re-login with the SAME semantic claims but signed by the OLD key. If Vault still accepts the old-key token, verification policy is not applied to the consumed proof (stale trust set).
finding.description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_oldkey_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_oldkey_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Vault accepted a JWT signed by a removed/old key after trust-anchor rotation (stale verification policy applied to consumed proof)

sequence.description: Direct JWT login: simulate signing-key rotation by changing jwt_validation_pubkeys after a successful control login, then re-login with the SAME semantic claims but signed by the OLD key. sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I1: After trust-anchor rotation, Vault must verify JWT signatures against the updated trust source; tokens signed by removed keys (even with identical semantic claims) must be rejected.

Evaluation: user_A_replay_after_tighten_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Replay of an old JWT (iat far older than new max_age) was accepted after freshness tightening; indicates stale freshness enforcement.

Assertion FAILED: user_A_slightly_expired_attack_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_A_slightly_expired_attack_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Slightly expired JWT was accepted (likely due to leeway sentinel default behavior); freshness/anti-replay expectation violated for expired artifacts.
